text:
Calgary lost its best defenseman to a freak injury this weekend and won anyway, which is a fair summary of how the Flames' season has gone: not pretty, still hanging around. Kevin Bahl ruptured his Achilles tendon in an off-ice warmup and is out for the season. He led the team in ice time, and he and Simon Nemec were the pair Ryan Huska leaned on most, more than 200 minutes together. Replacing that is the problem of the year.

The other story is in net. Devin Cooley has won his last five starts with a .945 save percentage, 7.0 goals better than his shots deserved, and Dustin Wolf has had the rougher stretch. That's the kind of run that makes a coach's decision for him for a while.

The underlying numbers are thin. The Flames take about 46% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), the power play produces 0.38 expected goals a game, and no forward line we track is above water in chances. At 8-9-1 and 17 points, our simulations give them a 12% playoff chance and a projection near 80 points. Joel Farabee has been the most dangerous forward lately, and Matvei Gridin is the young player worth following. What to watch: who absorbs Bahl's minutes, and whether Cooley can keep stopping everything while the team in front of him figures out how to create chances.
